title: VQC trained on 10% of the training split — WDBC
objective: Test whether the gap shrinks as the training set grows (H4).
description: Base VQC trained on 10% of the training split. The full curve (10–100%) for all models appears in Fig. 3 of the paper; only the values stated in the text are stored here.
observations: With 10% of the data, the gap of the VQC exceeded that of the MLP on all four datasets (by 0.049 to 0.118) and its test AUC was lower (−0.049 to −0.038).
limitations: Intermediate points of Fig. 3 are not tabulated in the paper and are not reproduced here.

title: VQC trained for 25 epochs — WDBC
objective: Test whether part of the gap is an artifact of the training budget (H5).
description: Base VQC trained for 25 epochs instead of 200.
observations: Between 25 and 800 epochs the gap of the VQC rose on every dataset, as it did for the MLP. Training from 200 to 800 epochs raised the gap on the synthetic data and Blood Transfusion (+0.009 and +0.010) without improving the test AUC.
limitations: Only the 25- and 800-epoch gaps of the VQC are stated numerically in the paper.

title: VQC on four learned features — WDBC
objective: Test whether a representation learned by a classical teacher reduces the gap, and how much of any change comes from the classical encoder rather than the circuit (H6).
description: VQC trained on the four features learned by the classical encoder, scaled to [−π, π].
observations: The VQC on learned features was much worse than the linear head, partly an encoding artifact: 82% to 99% of the learned values lay in the outer 10% of their range, and [−π, π] maps both ends to the same state.

title: Classical encoder trained jointly with a linear head
objective: Compare a fixed four-component PCA representation with a learned 32 → 4 encoder, using quantum and classical heads.
description: Separately trained classical encoder with a linear (logistic) head, trained jointly.
observations: Essentially perfect training AUC; its train–validation difference (0.0655) approached that of the jointly trained encoder–VQC (0.0778), with substantially worse validation log loss (0.7585).

title: Staged neural quantum embedding, fidelity similarity (NQE-Q)
objective: Test whether supervised pair geometry in the embedding improves downstream classification.
description: 50 epochs of pairwise geometry training with quantum product-state fidelity k_Q, then 50 epochs of VQC classifier fitting.
observations: Exposed a sharper readout discrepancy: logistic regression on the same frozen embedding reached a higher validation AUC (see the same-embedding readout comparison).
limitations: Staged and joint procedures use different total update budgets and expose the encoder to different gradients, so this comparison does not isolate a schedule effect. k_Q is classically computable for the product-RY encoding; no quantum computational advantage is implied.

title: Logistic regression on the frozen NQE-Q embedding
objective: Compare a quantum readout and a logistic readout fitted on the same frozen four-dimensional embedding (staged quantum-fidelity training).
description: Logistic regression fitted on the same frozen four-dimensional embedding used by the NQE-Q VQC readout. The values come from a retrospective analysis that reused stored probabilities.
observations: LR improved validation AUC in 10 of 15 paired fold–seed cells, but the 15 cells do not represent independent patients or independent confirmation.
limitations: The VQC and LR differ in function family, output intercept and scale, optimizer and regularization. Equal coordinates do not make this a parameter-matched causal comparison. No significance test is claimed.
